title: The marathon legend is not in the main source. Herodotus never mentions a run from Marathon to
description:
Herodotus never mentions a run from Marathon to Athens. He does not mention a dying messenger either.

The generals sent a runner from Athens to Sparta, who arrived the day after he left. He reported that the god Pan had appeared to him.

The messenger sent to Sparta before the Battle of Marathon, named in some sources as Pheidippides.

The Spartathlon distance from Athens to Sparta, run every year since 1983.

The first known Marathon to Athens account is by Plutarch, centuries after the battle. He names a herald called Thersippus or Eukles. Lucian later names the runner Philippides.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pheidippides (read): established that Herodotus describes an Athenian messenger and professional long distance runner sent to Sparta before the Battle of Marathon in 490 BC, and does not mention a run from Marathon to Athens or a death; that the first known account of a Marathon to Athens run is by Plutarch (46 to 120 AD), who names a herald called Thersippus or Eukles; that Lucian, about a century later, names the runner Philippides and has him die; that the Spartathlon is 246 km and has been run annually since 1983; and that Michel Bréal, inspired by Browning's 1879 poem, proposed a marathon race for the 1896 Olympics.
- https://cts.perseids.org/read/greekLit/tlg0016/tlg001/perseus-eng2/6.105.3-6.106.3 (read): Herodotus 6.105 to 6.106 in translation; established that Philippides was in Sparta the day after leaving Athens, sent by the generals, that he reported Pan had appeared to him, and that the only running mentioned is from Athens to Sparta, with no run from Marathon to Athens.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon (read): established that the first Olympic marathon took place on 10 April 1896, won by Spyridon Louis in 2 hours 58 minutes 50 seconds, and that historians dispute the legend because Herodotus describes a run from Athens to Sparta and back and nothing about Marathon to Athens.
